Human Inter-Rater Reliability (IRR) Ceiling Benchmark

Source: R/human_irr.R
human_irr.Rd

Computes human-vs-human inter-rater reliability across two or more human annotators in either wide format (rater_cols = c("h1", "h2", "h3")) or long format (id_col, rater_col, score_col), and optionally benchmarks an LLM's calibration_metrics() directly against the human inter-rater ceiling.

Usage

human_irr(
  data,
  rater_cols = NULL,
  id_col = NULL,
  rater_col = NULL,
  score_col = NULL,
  type = c("auto", "continuous", "categorical", "ordinal"),
  llm_calibration = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame containing human ratings in wide or long format.

rater_cols

Character vector of column names for wide-format ratings (at least 2 human rater columns). Mutually exclusive with (id_col, rater_col, score_col).

id_col

Unit identifier column name for long-format ratings.

rater_col

Human rater identifier column name for long-format ratings.

score_col

Score/label column name for long-format ratings.

type

Measurement scale: "auto" (numeric -> "continuous", factor/character/logical -> "categorical"), "continuous", "categorical", or "ordinal".

llm_calibration

Optional "llm_calibration" object returned by calibration_metrics() to benchmark LLM-human agreement directly against the human inter-rater ceiling.

conf_level

Confidence level for Fleiss's \(\kappa\) CI. Default 0.95.

na.rm

Logical; drop units/rows with insufficient ratings. Default TRUE.

Value

An S3 object of class "llm_human_irr" containing:

  • metrics: tibble of human-vs-human reliability statistics.

  • benchmark: tibble comparing LLM calibration against the human ceiling (or NULL if llm_calibration is NULL).

  • type, n_units, n_raters, balanced, method_used.

Details

  • Continuous ratings: two-way random absolute agreement \(\mathrm{ICC}(A,1)\) (single rater) and \(\mathrm{ICC}(A,k)\) (average of \(k\) raters), consistency \(\mathrm{ICC}(C,1)\) and \(\mathrm{ICC}(C,k)\) (using lme4::lmer REML automatically when ratings are unbalanced/missing), plus mean pairwise Pearson \(r\), Spearman \(\rho\), MAE, and RMSE.

  • Categorical / ordinal ratings: pairwise percent agreement, unweighted and weighted Cohen's \(\kappa\) (when \(k = 2\)), Fleiss's \(\kappa\) (for any \(k \ge 2\) with analytic SE and 95% CI), and multi-rater Krippendorff's \(\alpha\) (nominal or ordinal distance metric, supporting arbitrary missing ratings).

Examples

set.seed(10)
true_z <- rnorm(60, mean = 4, sd = 1.2)
wide_df <- tibble::tibble(
  h1 = true_z + rnorm(60, sd = 0.40),
  h2 = true_z + rnorm(60, sd = 0.45),
  h3 = true_z + rnorm(60, sd = 0.42),
  llm = 0.2 + 0.9 * true_z + rnorm(60, sd = 0.48)
)
cal <- calibration_metrics(wide_df, pred_col = "llm", truth_col = "h1")
irr <- human_irr(wide_df, rater_cols = c("h1", "h2", "h3"), llm_calibration = cal)
irr
#> 
#> ── Human Inter-Rater Reliability Ceiling (continuous) 
#> Units: 60 | Human raters: 3 | Balanced: TRUE | Method: two_way_anova
#> ICC(A,1) = 0.877 | ICC(A,k) = 0.955 | ICC(C,1) = 0.877 | Mean r = 0.880 |
#> Pairwise RMSE = 0.584
#> LLM Calibration vs. Human Inter-Rater Ceiling:
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   metric       human_ceiling llm_vs_human      gap pct_of_ceiling
#>   <chr>                <dbl>        <dbl>    <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 ICC(A,1)             0.877        0.844 -0.0330            96.2
#> 2 ICC(C,1)             0.877        0.850 -0.0274            96.9
#> 3 Pearson r            0.880        0.851 -0.0292            96.7
#> 4 Spearman rho         0.853        0.845 -0.00758           99.1
